title: Hyperframes inspiration
description:
## Purpose and decision
Make VideoML an exciting, practical home for frame-driven motion graphics by reproducing the breadth of the Hyperframes effects catalog in VideoML and showcasing it on the VideoML website. Reuse or migrate suitable Babulus animation demos before rebuilding existing work.

This issue body is the canonical initiative document. Keep rationale, milestone status, architectural decisions, scope changes, and coverage links here. Epics describe milestones; stories express observable behavior; tasks capture concrete implementation work. Do not create a competing planning document.

## Product boundary
VideoML owns the standard, frame-based timing contract, player, reusable effects, and standalone visual demos/catalog. It remains animation-framework agnostic: any library that can produce reproducible states for requested frames is eligible. GSAP is not mandatory and adopting Hyperframes's renderer is not an initiative requirement.

VideoML includes standard voiceover features migrated/formalized from Babulus, with open local synthesis based on Auritus and its supported local TTS models. Voice, cues, timing, pronunciation, and portable audio artifacts are part of this effort. The open local path must not require paid providers, Babulus accounts, or cloud credentials. Model-specific licenses and hardware requirements remain documented.

Auritus owns reusable speech/model capabilities; improve it through this integration rather than creating a fork. Babulus becomes an optional paid rendering platform with no vendor lock-in: portable VideoML source, assets, generated audio/timing, and rendering configuration remain usable locally. Selected Babulus animation demos also move into VideoML. This supersedes the earlier proposal that Babulus exclusively owns voiceover.

## Technical baseline and evidence
Both projects capture browser visuals and encode with FFmpeg. Hyperframes adds useful frame adapters, custom shader/compositing code, ready-made effects, and authoring guidance. Its visuals do not establish a fundamentally higher rendering ceiling than VideoML. Borrow the useful effects and patterns while preserving VideoML's architecture.

Inspected Hyperframes revision: 28181602f (local checkout, 2026-10-30). Relevant sources: packages/core/src/runtime/adapters/, packages/shader-transitions/, registry/components/, registry/blocks/, docs/concepts/frame-adapters.mdx. Verify and pin the complete revision when building the inventory; avoid treating a changing catalog count as a fixed target.

Babulus already contains examples/animation-*, features/animation_systems.feature, packages/renderer/src/components/registry.ts, and Studio docs preview mounts. Its AGENTS.md identifies the extracted VideoML repositories as authoritative for VideoML code. Current apps/studio-web/package.json declares @videoml/player and @videoml/stdlib ^1.0.0; older instructions describe local file aliases. Resolve actual consumption before migration.

## Catalog scope
Target the full pinned Hyperframes catalog, not only a few showcase effects. Start with an exhaustive source inventory and explicit per-entry mapping/status. Deliver in category batches: framework demos, shader transitions, typography, particles, motion trails, charts/data, UI/device scenes, overlays, camera motion, and 3D/procedural effects. Record all gaps and justified deferrals. A visual example counts as complete only with reusable implementation, runnable source, documentation, and verification evidence.

The public catalog lives in VideoML/videoml-org. It provides browse/search/filter, stable effect pages, live frame-scrubbable demos, adjustable parameters, copyable VideoML examples, dependency requirements, source links, and provenance. Visual-only examples must run without Babulus accounts, voice credentials, or HeyGen hosted rendering.

## Milestones
1. M1 — Establish ownership, catalog inventory, and frame conformance — videoml-c22afb
2. M2 — Bring reusable animation demos into VideoML — videoml-db06d1
3. M3 — Add deterministic shader transitions — videoml-a0007f
4. M4 — Build out the reusable effects catalog — videoml-be414b
5. M5 — Publish the VideoML website effects catalog — videoml-eb659c
6. M6 — Verify visual quality and Babulus adoption — videoml-10636d
7. M7 — Standardize voiceover and integrate open local Auritus TTS — videoml-692db2
8. M8 — Deliver portable Babulus rendering with local-first AWS Batch fallback — videoml-49cdfa
9. M9 — Isolate AWS costs and gate cloud rendering with spend controls — videoml-e832b8

Use the packet dependency graph below for dispatch. Do not infer execution order from milestone numbers.

## Definition of completion
- The pinned catalog has an auditable mapping; every target is verified or explicitly deferred with a reason and follow-up issue. Full parity is claimed only if the inventory supports it.
- Public VideoML catalog examples are runnable, inspectable, and reusable from shared packages.
- Repeated, backward, random, and parallel frame evaluation is reproducible within recorded tolerances; preview/export parity is demonstrated under pinned environments.
- Existing Babulus functionality remains usable, and shared effects work in a narrated Babulus fixture.
- Source/license provenance and asset dependencies accompany reused implementations.
- No required migration to HeyGen services, no mandatory animation framework, and no proprietary dependency for standard VideoML voiceover or project export.

## Current status
Accepted: P00–P05, P09, P13–P15. Foundation PRs, Auritus PR91/92, shared demos stdlib PR2, particles stdlib PR3, and coordinated P15 specification PR2/toolchain PR3/player PR2/CLI PR3 have merged. P15 has exact PCM assembly, cache identity, normalized source IDs, frozen playback/export and real browser/FFmpeg evidence using explicitly fake speech. Real Kokoro is still P16. Particle entries are implemented; catalog verified count remains zero pending release gates.

P06 Babulus migration passed its required Studio CI mirror using existing Node20.20.2 and verified real Amplify outputs, plus10 behavior scenarios. The vendored package matches stdlib source4fb36e9a994f1c382efffa3fdabd0d51c63dc623. Its commit/push approval is pending under Babulus AGENTS; source remains uncommitted. Shared demo producer has landed and allseven local browser comparisons passed.

P10 echo-smear is in progress. The initial shape-only scope was rejected; the implementation now includes a frame-driven existing-DOM target adapter, with real browser review still finding and correcting cloning/visibility details. P16 preflight found the required Python3.12 local TTS/language dependencies installed and identified approximately328MB of pinned Kokoro model plus af_heart voice downloads. No model download/inference has yet occurred. Transfer the single heavy-operation slot explicitly between P10 browser tests and P16 setup/inference.

D16 resource controls remain active: at most two implementation writers, one heavy operation,8GiB free floor. User-approved global cache cleanup and removal of only task-created, fully verified Babulus dependency/build trees recovered capacity; retain unrelated scratch, source, package archives, real config and evidence. No new AWS account, cloud rendering or website deployment has occurred. Account mailbox remains rap+aws-babulus-videoml@endymion.com; alerts rap@endymion.com. P20a must prove renderer isolation before cloud rollout. Full catalog, shader compositor, website, real speech, portable bundles and paid rendering platform remain required.


## Binding implementation decisions (2026-10-30)
These decisions supersede vague alternatives in earlier planning text. Stories retain behavior; the ordered Terra packets below define implementation. Only the primary reviewer changes these decisions. Milestone numbers describe areas, not a mandatory serial order.

### D01 — Ownership and repository layout
Keep the six VideoML repositories; do not create a monorepo or replace Gatsby. specification owns normative prose and JSON schemas; toolchain owns compiler/render integration and test harnesses; stdlib owns reusable effects and their manifest; player owns interactive frame control; cli owns vml commands; videoml-org owns the Gatsby catalog. Auritus owns Python models and the local speech bridge. Babulus owns service auth, scheduling, billing ledger, and AWS deployment. Preserve the current renderer; do not switch to Hyperframes or Remotion. Published package boundaries replace relative imports across repositories. Use npm pack tarballs for cross-repo acceptance before release; never depend on a developer's absolute paths.

### D02 — Frame/effect contract
Add a framework-neutral EffectInstance interface in stdlib: mount(root, {width,height,fps,seed,assets}), seek(frame): Promise<void>, dispose(): void. Frame is a nonnegative integer; time is frame/fps; visibility intervals are [startFrame,endFrame). Effects support random/repeated/backward seeks and settle assets before completion. Pure time formulas or baked deterministic trajectories are allowed; ambient wall clock and unseeded random state are not. Register versioned effect IDs and validated JSON parameters. Share this effect implementation between player DOM mounting and renderer browser mounting; preserve existing React components with an adapter instead of rewriting all layouts. Add explicit seek/pause/dispose to player API. Never use HTML server rendering alone as proof that canvas/WebGL works.

### D03 — Initial demos and effect implementation
Migrate the existing AnimeHarnessDemo, ThreeOrbit, LottieBadge, D3BarChart, P5Particles, TextEffects and MixAndMatchDemo first. Keep old names as documented aliases for one minor release in Babulus. Then implement particle-text-dissolve, particle-image-reveal and echo-smear; port all shader registry entries as compositors with two timed scene textures. Use GSAP where upstream logic needs it but never require it for every effect. Adapt permissively licensed upstream implementation with retained notices; do not spend effort recreating an identical shader merely to avoid reuse. Do not copy unlicensed media: use a locally generated neutral fixture. Premium/network integrations become asset-parameterized offline examples, not hidden service dependencies. Unsupported hardware produces a named error or documented crossfade fallback, never a silent blank frame.

### D04 — Exhaustive catalog scope
Pin Hyperframes commit 28181602fe2d9ffa38474a6e8155a89909a7b8aa. Import registry/registry.json items and all directories under registry/components, blocks and examples; union with shader registry names and deduplicate using kind/name (not display title). Current directory baseline: 238 components, 210 blocks, 8 examples. Inventory must detect orphan directories or missing listed items and fail rather than dropping them. Store metadata under stdlib/catalog with schemaVersion, id, upstream commit/path, license/notice, dependency versions, category/tags, parameter schema, fixture paths, and planned/implemented/verified status. Keep marketing claims at the verified count. Full coverage is the target; any incompatible entry requires a primary-reviewer decision recorded in the initiative, not a Terra unilateral deferral.

### D05 — Website
Keep Gatsby 5 / React 18. Generate /catalog and /catalog/<id> from the shared manifest. Search name/description/tags; filter category and framework in URL query parameters. Use poster-first cards, no autoplay; detail page has play/pause, integer frame scrubber, parameter controls, reset, source/license links and copyable XML/TS. Preview trusted shipped examples in a dedicated iframe; do not execute arbitrary visitor input. Rebuild only on explicit parameter changes. Keyboard controls and reduced-motion default-to-paused are mandatory. Import data from packed stdlib; do not duplicate catalog data in the site. Load heavy frameworks on the detail page, not every listing card.

### D06 — Standard voiceover and local bridge
Use existing <voiceover>, <cue>, <voice>, <pause> semantics as the compatibility baseline; document them as draft standard v0.1, not a new unreviewed syntax. The default new-project provider is auritus, voice kokoro:af_heart, speed 1, seed 0. Visual-only documents instantiate no TTS provider. Keep paid providers as explicit choices; remove automatic missing-credential/CI-to-dry-run substitution. Test stubs require explicit dry-run configuration and must mark artifacts simulated.

Auritus already has auritus.speech.synthesize, Voice and SpeechOptions: wrap it, do not reimplement synthesis. Add python -m auritus.speech_bridge, a versioned newline-delimited JSON process protocol. Node spawns the configured Python executable with argv (no shell), keeps one process per generation run, serializes requests, and closes it at completion. stdout contains JSON only; diagnostics go to stderr. Requests: {protocol:1,id,op:'capabilities'|'synthesize',text?,voice?,speed?,seed?,outputDir?,voicesDir?}. Responses: {protocol:1,id,ok:true,result:{...}} or {protocol:1,id,ok:false,error:{code,message}}. Capabilities report installed/runtime readiness, backend/model identity and supported options without downloading a model. Synthesize writes speech.wav and speech.json atomically under a unique caller-provided segment directory, returns relative names, sampleRate, sampleCount, durationSec, segments and provenance. Errors: INVALID_REQUEST, BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE, MODEL_NOT_INSTALLED, UNSUPPORTED_OPTION, SYNTHESIS_FAILED; recoverable request failures return an error response and keep the process alive. Clean EOF shuts down with exit 0; only fatal protocol/process failure exits nonzero. Timeout kills the whole process group, invalidates the in-flight request, and removes its partial files; the caller fails the generation run instead of silently restarting. Node rejects protocol/id mismatch, malformed JSON, missing/escaping paths, timeout after 300s per segment, and nonzero exit. A model setup command is explicit; generation must never download silently or fall back to paid synthesis. CI mocks protocol explicitly; one real Kokoro smoke run is a release gate.

### D07 — Timing, cache and reproducibility
Synthesize each voice text segment separately. Toolchain inserts explicit pauses as PCM silence rounded to nearest sample; do not approximate arbitrary pauses with Auritus fixed break markers. Derive duration from decoded sample count, then resolve cue layout; frame visibility uses floor(startSec*fps) / ceil(endSec*fps), with exact audio sample offsets retained. Reject overlapping narration on the same voice track unless explicitly configured as separate tracks. Auritus segment timing is block timing, never claim word alignment.

Use a separate VideoML cache v1 keyed by SHA256 of canonical sorted JSON containing final pronunciation-expanded text, provider/backend/model and resolved model revision, Auritus version, reference audio/transcript content digests, voice, speed, seed, and output audio settings. Preserve Auritus remote content_hash and speech request_key unchanged as provenance. If model revision cannot be resolved, disable cache reuse for that request and report why. Emit/verify PCM audio SHA256. Rendering uses frozen audio; regenerating speech across hardware is not promised bit-identical. Exact pronunciation aliases are supported everywhere; phoneme directives require an advertised provider capability and otherwise fail explicitly. Retain original and expanded text for audit.

### D08 — Portable bundle v1
A directory or ZIP contains videoml-project.json, source/, assets/, audio/, timing/, dependencies.lock.json and notices/. Manifest fields: schemaVersion:1, projectId, entry, width,height,fps,durationFrames, seed, toolchainVersion, assets[{path,sha256,mediaType}], audio/timing paths, effects[{id,version}], and pinned dependency/font versions. JSON schema disallows unsupported version and unknown required semantics. Paths are relative POSIX paths, no .., absolute paths, symlinks or missing/hash-mismatched files. Export contains generated narration and timing so rendering never needs TTS credentials. No network fetch during frame capture. Hosted preparation and rendering also have no network once the supervisor has staged the validated bundle. Trusted CLI projects may compile TS during preparation; hosted service only runs its pinned worker image and allowlisted dependency versions. The hosted pilot accepts only declarative XML with built-in/approved effect IDs and validated data parameters: reject scripts, event handlers, custom components, executable expressions, HTML injection, external URLs and TS entrypoints. Local CLI still supports trusted custom code; hosted validation clearly explains this supported subset. No arbitrary package installs or setup hooks. Separate the credentialed download/upload supervisor from the unprivileged renderer; materialize the validated bundle first, launch the renderer without credentials, metadata access or network, then upload verified output. Bundled fonts/images/video/audio only; sanitize SVG external/script content and reject unsupported active formats. ZIP limits: compressed <=250 MiB, expanded <=1 GiB, <=10,000 files, max 250 MiB per file, reject duplicate normalized paths/symlinks/absolute/traversal paths before extraction; stream enforce limits to prevent ZIP bombs. User data must never become code in an approved effect. Export/import must not require a Babulus account; file bundles remain useful after service access ends.

### D09 — Local-first state machine
Use Babulus job API as the only authority. Persist QUEUED_LOCAL -> CLAIMED_LOCAL or CLOUD_RESERVED -> CLAIMED_CLOUD -> SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELLED; FAILED attempts can requeue only via the bounded retry policy. deadline=createdAt+300 seconds. Heartbeat every 15s; lease 60s; maximum attempt wall time 1200s, renewed leases cannot extend this. Atomically compare status, lease expiry and monotonically increasing generation token on each ownership transition. Local claim racing deadline competes with CLOUD_RESERVED CAS; only one wins. No late local claim after cloud reservation. Write artifacts under jobId/attemptId/generation; publish by conditional completion matching owner/generation. Stale worker uploads are not authoritative. Cancellation fences all old tokens before stopping work.

Each job permits at most 2 attempts total and at most 1 cloud attempt. Local worker crash may retry once locally or fall back after the deadline; never loop forever. Batch retryStrategy attempts=1. Submission uses a persisted outbox/reservation ID. On SubmitJob timeout/unknown result, never blindly resubmit: reconcile jobs by deterministic attempt name/tag, choose one canonical job, cancel duplicates, and keep reservation held. If unresolved after 10 minutes, stop new cloud admission and surface operator reconciliation. Exactly-once submission cannot be assumed from Batch API.


#### D09a — Authoritative transitions and transaction boundary
Job records persist jobId, tenantId, status, createdAt, deadline, attemptCount, cloudAttemptCount, generation, owner, leaseExpiresAt, absoluteAttemptDeadline, cancellationGeneration, outboxId and canonicalBatchJobId. Server time is authoritative; clients cannot set lease deadlines.
- QUEUED_LOCAL -> CLAIMED_LOCAL: conditional claim increments attemptCount and generation; requires attemptCount<2 and no cloud reservation. Creates 60s lease and 1200s absolute deadline.
- CLAIMED_LOCAL -> SUCCEEDED: completion checks token, lease and uncancelled status, then atomically publishes artifact digest/manifest. Heartbeat extends lease only up to absolute deadline.
- CLAIMED_LOCAL -> QUEUED_LOCAL: expired lease or retryable failure fences old generation, clears owner, preserves original fallback deadline; allowed only when attemptCount<2 and cloudAttemptCount=0. If exhausted or fatal validation failure, transition FAILED. Another local claim is allowed before cloud reservation; the cloud CAS may win once deadline passed.
- QUEUED_LOCAL -> CLOUD_RESERVED: one DynamoDB TransactWrite checks grace deadline, enabled policy/drill permission, no cancellation, attemptCount<2, cloudAttemptCount=0, fresh price and limits; increments attempts/generation, reserves operator day/month budget+global slot+customer credit, and writes a unique PENDING outbox entry. All financial/job/outbox items are in transaction-compatible DynamoDB tables in the same account/region. Nothing dispatches without this committed transaction. Idempotency key is jobId plus generation; repeat cannot double debit.
- CLOUD_RESERVED remains reserved while outbox submits/reconciles. It has no local claim lease. A Batch worker can transition to CLAIMED_CLOUD only with the canonical Batch job ID and generation; duplicate jobs cannot claim. Start sets lease/deadline bounded by Batch timeout. Supervisor handles heartbeat independently of untrusted content.
- CLOUD_RESERVED -> FAILED/CANCELLED when refusal/no-submit proof or watchdog concludes; release operator reservation only with proof no paid submit. Unknown submission retains reservation and slot until reconciled and trips admission stop. No blind retry. Customer credit refunds when failure is authoritative.
- CLAIMED_CLOUD -> SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELLED: conditional finalization; release global slot only after worker termination/result verified, retain operator admission charge, settle/refund customer credit exactly once. Cloud crash/expiry is terminal (cloudAttemptCount max 1); never return to local queue automatically after cloud reservation.
- Any nonterminal -> CANCELLED: transaction increments generation and records cancellation; authoritative cancellation wins against a later completion, completion already committed remains SUCCEEDED. Stop children and cancel/terminate remote jobs; do not free a slot while an old job can still run. Idempotent outbox reconciler recovers orphaned pending entries after coordinator crash.
Fault tests inject crashes before/after transaction, before/after submit and before/after completion; replay must not double charge, launch blindly, publish stale output or release an uncertain reservation.

### D10 — AWS implementation and conservative pilot defaults
Dedicated member account name Babulus-VideoML, region us-east-1. Use TypeScript CDK under Babulus/infra/rendering and AWS Batch Fargate Linux x86_64, pinned Chrome/FFmpeg worker image, 4 vCPU/8 GiB, software WebGL verified by fixtures, no GPU fleet for video v1. Default cloud enabled=false. One cloud job at a time globally; vCPU capacity 4. Output limit 1920x1080, 30fps, 60 seconds/1800 frames, 250 MiB bundled input. Longer/larger projects remain supported locally but hosted pilot rejects them. Batch runtime timeout 1200s plus 10-minute queued/starting watchdog. Private S3, signed URLs, SSE, task role only job-scoped broker operations; no inbound worker ports, no NAT gateway for pilot (document limited outbound setup paths). Frame capture has no network. Separate cloud speech is not in v1: generate/freeze voice locally before submit.

Babulus currently launches ECS Fargate immediately through amplify/functions/render-trigger. Replace that behavior with enqueue/outbox only; a single coordinator owns Batch admission. Do not introduce a second paid launch path. Disable old ECS launch before enabling Batch; rollback disables new cloud dispatch rather than reenabling immediate ECS. Existing in-flight work drains/cancels through an explicit migration report. Do not delete buckets or customer outputs as cleanup.

### D11 — Cost accounting and emergency controls
Pilot cloud admission uses integer micro-USD transactional reservations: $2 per cloud attempt, global $10/day and $50/calendar month UTC, 5 cloud attempts/day per tenant, 1 global concurrent cloud slot. Reject any job whose conservative current compute/storage/transfer estimate exceeds $2 or whose pricing snapshot is missing/older than 7 days. Reservation is a control ceiling, not an AWS bill guarantee. Never release a full reservation merely because a job failed; retain the day's/month's admission charge after any confirmed or uncertain paid submission. Release only if proven no submission occurred. Refund commercial customer credit separately. This bounds admitted attempts without trusting late billing data. Alert on 50/80/100% of $50 monthly account-wide AWS budget, plus daily anomaly signals. Tag project/job/attempt/tenant/service; report all services including non-rendering infrastructure. Running cost controls cannot promise an exact invoice cap.

Emergency stop: atomically disable admission and fence outstanding attempts, disable Batch queue, cancel queued jobs, terminate STARTING/RUNNING jobs, and reconcile until none remain. Preserve artifacts, record actor/reason. A soft pause only stops new jobs. Local-only work remains available in both cases. Cost-reservation service unavailable or inconsistent => no cloud submission. Auto-enabling after an alert is prohibited.

### D12 — Commercial pilot
Babulus is paid for managed cloud rendering; portable CLI and local execution remain free of Babulus fees. Pilot price is $2 per successful cloud render within the v1 limits; local and failed/cancelled renders cost the customer $0. Use an operator-invoiced prepaid USD credit ledger initially, no payment processor integration. Reserve customer credit before cloud dispatch, settle exactly once only after verified output, refund failed/cancelled jobs. Display the price and local-first/cloud-disabled policy before submission. Local-only is default; cloud fallback requires explicit per-project enablement. Pricing is versioned on each job and must not change mid-job. Do not store card data. Automated checkout/subscriptions are explicitly outside this pilot.

### D13 — Deployment facts are not design choices
Do not invent AWS account IDs, root mailboxes, OU IDs, payer access, billing contacts, or credentials. The account packet discovers organization/account conventions read-only, uses Babulus-VideoML/us-east-1, reuses an existing dedicated account if uniquely verified, and emits a deployment manifest. A unique company-controlled mailbox and verified budget recipient must be supplied/validated before CreateAccount; lacking them blocks only account creation/cloud enablement, not local implementation or CDK synth. Use the organization's current application OU and federated deployment roles; never long-lived IAM users. Record exact facts in a gitignored local manifest and account ID/region in nonsecret deployment outputs. Provisioning is a later explicit implementation/deployment operation, not performed by this plan update.

### D14 — Verification thresholds and shipping gates
Standard fixture environment: pinned Linux x86_64 Chromium/FFmpeg image, bundled fonts, 1280x720 at 30fps, seed 0. Capture frames 0,1,midpoint,last and both sides of every transition boundary; repeated/reversed/random requests plus two worker partitions. Same environment deterministic screenshots require exact decoded RGBA equality. Preview/export comparison allows <=0.5% pixels differing by >8/255 in any RGB channel; all failures require reviewer inspection, never threshold widening by a worker. Cross-platform GPU differences use separately reviewed baselines; do not claim byte equality across GPUs. Audio sample-count timing differs by <=1 sample in PCM assembly and <=1 frame in final muxed duration. Test silent, narrated, shader, particle, trail, nested and cancelled fixtures. Inspect actual browser output and encoded video; successful HTML or build alone is not sufficient.

Every packet defines npm run lint/test where scripts exist; add scoped npm scripts for new conformance suites, and run required repo checks. Auritus behavior changes start with features/*.feature and use make check. Babulus uses Gherkin and its documented CI mirror for Studio edits. Website build and browser checks follow relevant site skills at implementation time. No effect counts verified before screenshots/clip evidence and primary review. No cloud pilot enablement before fault-injection and shutdown drills in the dedicated account. P26 uses operator-authorized drillEnabled=true restricted to one nominated tenant and immutable fixture SHA256 for at most one job concurrently and three attempts total (including failure drills), expiring after two hours. It goes through the identical D09a/D11/D12 transaction; operator funds test credit and labels it non-customer. productionCloudEnabled stays false. Disable drills immediately after evidence collection; exhausted budget does not bypass controls.

### D15 — Terra dispatch and review
Primary agent dispatches gpt-6.1-terra explicitly, one bounded packet per worker with fork_turns=none, issue body + required contract sections + exact repository/paths. No more than one writer per repository/worktree; use isolated worktrees when parallel edits overlap. Workers read applicable AGENTS, mark only assigned issue in_progress, write behavior tests first where required, implement within scope, run checks, and return diff/commands/artifacts/remaining failures. They do not change contracts, loosen thresholds, deploy/publish, close issues, or mark themselves approved. Primary reviews diff and executes focused acceptance, checks visual/audio evidence, then closes accepted work or returns concrete repairs. A second Terra read-only review is required for TTS/cache, portability, claims, billing, and AWS controls. Follow each repository's commit rules; planning does not authorize product release or cloud enablement. Blocked prerequisite => choose another ready packet, never fabricate success. Failed real-model/hardware/cloud tests remain visibly unverified.

P12 remains open until copied XML executes actual effects in a clean consumer and matches direct preview.

### D03b — Complete shader adaptation and XML integration
P08 covers all14 pinned shaders and owns stdlib/player/toolchain after P12a releases those repositories. Names: domain-warp, ridged-burn, whip-pan, sdf-iris, ripple-waves, gravitational-lens, cinematic-zoom, chromatic-split, glitch, swirl-vortex, thermal-distortion, flash-through-white, cross-warp-morph, light-leak. Adapt exact permissively licensed formulas and required uniforms, retaining notices. Typed optional RGB triples accent/dark/bright each contain three finite0..1 numbers; defaults [1,0.6,0.2], [0.4,0.15,0], [1,0.85,0.5]. Resolution is derived from validated composition dimensions, never user-overridden inconsistent uniforms. Optional backgroundColor is #RRGGBB and explicitly composites both input textures over that color before use; absence preserves input textures. Endpoints return exact input textures (or explicitly background-composited textures); interior output follows pinned shader math including its alpha semantics. Do not claim all opaque-interior upstream effects preserve transparent alpha throughout; crossfade keeps correct premultiplied alpha. Test transparent endpoints and explicit background behavior separately from opaque upstream reference vectors.

Progress uses the resolved frozen transition interval and composition-absolute frame. Default is linear. Preserve explicit XML ease using existing GSAP-compatible named easing in the consumer bridge, evaluate as a pure function once, clamp the result to0..1, and pass to the shared compositor; unknown easing is a named error, never silent linear substitution. Endpoints bypass easing and shader distortion. The core compositor may accept a pure easing callback; no global wallclock or mandatory framework ownership is introduced.

Actual XML transition effect and props must reach P07 compositor via resolved fromSceneId/toSceneId and capture providers. Source IDs must resolve, both scenes advance at each frame, missing capture provider fails explicitly unless named opt-in crossfade is selected. No CSS-stack fallback masquerades as shader rendering. Add registry descriptors and real copiedXML integration tests for all14, exact sameenvironment repeat/random/boundaries, sampled upstream reference comparisons, named hardware fallback and resource cleanup. Website consumes a frozen integration package and equivalent scene assets; full encodedLinux release checks stay P28.

### D05b — Declarative local effect assets
P12a adds optional root-level <assets><asset id="font" src="assets/Geist-Latin.woff2" media-type="font/woff2"/></assets> (and image) declarations. IDs are unique asset-map keys; declarations are metadata, never timeline components. Relative POSIX src paths resolve against the source XML directory; reject absolute paths, backslashes, traversal, URL schemes/query/fragments and any realpath escape or special file. No implicit network downloads. Keep explicit programmatic effectAssets as an override only when its identity does not conflict with a declaration; ambiguity fails.

Generation copies declared bytes to content-addressed asset files adjacent to the generated script and emits script.meta.assets entries {id,path,mediaType,sha256}, with paths relative to that script directory. No absolute source paths in generated artifacts. CLI pipeline passes dirname(scriptOut) as the render asset base; CLI render passes dirname(scriptPath). Node render callers must supply assetBaseDir when manifest assets exist, or receive a named error. Read/verify actual bytes and materialize data/blob URLs before browser capture; browser frame capture itself performs no network fetch. Preserve frozen timing and source IDs, excluding assets/asset metadata from timed-node normalization. P17 includes these files and rewrites paths within the portable manifest.

Browser player accepts assetBaseUrl for XML declarations, defaulting to the containing document base URL; fetch same-origin relative resources during preparation, verify readable status/type and settle bytes before first seek. An XML-string caller can instead provide matching pre-resolved local blob/data effectAssets; declaration identity and any expected hash remain checked. Fetch cancellation follows player disposal, failures reject seek, and never silently replace missing fonts/images. Website serves owned matching assets and copied XML with relative asset paths plus a documented directory layout. For initial font/image effect assets, enforce <=32 declarations, <=16MiB each and <=64MiB total before base64/decode; other media types are not silently treated as image/font. Broader video/media support is an explicit future catalog-adapter extension, not a change to D08 bundle limits.

### Catalog inventory correction — unquoted shader key
Primary verified the pinned shader registry contains 14 keys, including unquoted `glitch` at packages/shader-transitions/src/shaders/registry.ts:144. The initial importer omitted that unquoted key. Exhaustive scope is 456 registry entries plus 14 shaders = 470 catalog entries. P08 includes shader/glitch and repairs the importer with a regression for unquoted keys; retain existing implementation/provenance metadata when regenerating. The 92 non-shader catalog batches are unchanged. Earlier 13/469 counts were incomplete inventory, not an authorized scope reduction.

### D08b — Local Chromium IPC candidate (not production acceptance)
Actual Linux ARM probes established FFmpeg compatibility but Chromium requires anonymous IPC. Primary and independent review authorize testing AF_UNIX socketpair only with protocol0, STREAM/SEQPACKET and CLOEXEC/NONBLOCK flags, plus sendmsg/recvmsg. Named/abstract socket creation/connect/bind/listen/accept and INET remain denied, as do sendto/recvfrom/mmsg, external FD acquisition, process inspection, namespace and group escape. Safety depends on verified FIFO stdio, close_range, unique UID, cleared capabilities and mandatory Landlock; open descriptors are not revoked by Landlock. Prove positive forked SCM_RIGHTS of sandbox-owned files and negative external socket/FD/proc/pidfd cases before real browser acceptance. Local paired Chromium tests may explicitly use --no-sandbox in both baseline and restricted commands: the outer kernel boundary must contain native renderer code, and this flag is never a silent fallback or production approval. Normal builds remain ISOLATION_UNAVAILABLE. Actual Chromium process-tree cancellation and exact Fargate x86 whole-task termination remain required.

D08b correction after implementation review: AF_UNIX SOCK_DGRAM remains denied. Unrestricted sendmsg can address an external pathname/abstract datagram socket through msg_name without connect/sendto, so anonymous socketpair alone is insufficient for DGRAM. This was caught before executing the candidate. Require real external listeners and negative addressed-sendmsg/SCM_RIGHTS tests for allowed connected STREAM/SEQPACKET pairs, plus explicit bind/listen/accept/mmsg denial. If Chromium needs DGRAM, fail closed and return for architecture review; do not permit it based on compatibility pressure.

### P08a website shader handoff
P08a videoml-0e01d3 follows accepted P08 and extends P12 with all14 interactive shader previews and matching standalone XML/assets; website catalog becomes470. Use two shared registered moving effects (echo-smear and particle-text-dissolve), composition1280x720/30fps/seed0/4s, scenes0–3s and2–4s, transition2–3s, native pixel providers matching renderer scene backgrounds and local timing. All14 copied XML previews require CLI parity at frames60/75/90 before acceptance. Only selected preview mounts. Packet contains controls, lifecycle, asset, provenance and evidence requirements. This is required before P28; no verified counts or deployment claims are implied.

### D08c — Secure portable bundle filesystem operations
P17 ships a narrow Python3.9+ helper as package data for secure directory traversal/staging/publication on macOS/Linux. It is an explicit local runtime prerequisite with a trusted executable override, never auto-downloaded. Missing required Python/OS primitives fails BUNDLE_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE. Invoke with argv and a bounded data-only JSON protocol, never shell/source execution. Anchor root and destination-parent traversal with held directory FDs and O_DIRECTORY/O_NOFOLLOW; reject symlinks, hardlinked regular files, specials, path/case/NFC collisions and changing size/count limits. Copy from opened FDs into an owned0700 stage using directory-relative O_EXCL creation; hash copied bytes and validate only stage. Bounded process output/timeout/cancellation must reap helper and clean only owned stage. Atomically publish to an absent target using verified no-replace rename: Linux renameat2 RENAME_NOREPLACE or Darwin renameatx_np RENAME_EXCL through a narrow libc wrapper. Ordinary overwrite-capable rename is insufficient; unsupported capability fails closed. ZIP parsing still validates strict headers, CRC, limits and paths and writes into the same private staging boundary. Test root/intermediate swaps, existing/appearing target, hardlinks/symlinks/specials, concurrent mutations and interruption with no partial publication. Publication trust boundary: the importing user/supervisor and publication hierarchy are trusted; this is safe ingestion of untrusted files, not isolation against malicious root or same-UID host processes. Require final parent owned by effective UID and not group/other writable, and held ancestors owned by root/current UID without untrusted write access (root-owned sticky ancestors may be accepted where child ownership protects rename). Hosted renderers use a distinct UID and never access the staging hierarchy. Reject insecure destinations. Verify stage-name inode against held stage FD and recheck parent identity as defense in depth; do not claim those checks close races from a malicious same-UID writer. Count all files AND directories with bounded path length/depth, stream directory enumeration, open source files nonblocking then verify regular-file identity, reject destination nested within source, and use nonblocking protocol reads with per-line/idle/total bounds. The helper is open portable implementation support, not a hosted dependency or vendor requirement.

### D02a — Catalog placement timing and authored snapshots
C001 preflight requires shared prerequisites P03a videoml-224803 and P03b videoml-8d09d9, sequenced after P17 releases shared checkouts. mountEffect provides frozen immutable composition start/end context; seek stays absolute. New local timelines subtract start before converting to seconds, while existing version1 effects keep accepted timing. Static authored scene snapshots use explicit sourceSceneId/sourceFrame references, dependency-cycle validation and optional injected providers; renderer uses P07 real browser capture. Missing capability errors explicitly, no fake DOM rasterization or monogram-only substitution. Bounds:4unique snapshots,depth8,4MP/4096px dimensions/16MiBPNG each,64MiB decoded aggregate,10s capture within existing job deadline. Snapshots have owned bitmap lifetime/cancellation and no cross-project cache. Exact contracts, scope, ordering and verification are in the two packets, which are mandatory C001 prerequisites.
D02a clarification: preserve floor(startSeconds*fps)/ceil(endSeconds*fps), copying bounds for visibility and context. Snapshot preparation is topological, single active source capture page, bounded PNG bridge between isolated pages and separately owned consumer bitmaps;64MiB encoded plus64MiB decoded across retained/in-flight copies. Fixed source frames are distinct cache keys, scene graph cycles fail.10s deadline spans queue/capture/transfer/decode. Detailed dependency/ownership tests are in P03b.
D08a selected composition identity: unreleased manifest v1 requires composition.id distinct from projectId. It must identify the selected authored composition and agree with generated script and any declared frozen timing composition identity. Multi-composition export requires explicit --composition ID; single composition may auto-select but always persists its exact ID. Import rejects missing, ambiguous or inconsistent identities before publication. Preserve P02 digest algorithm unchanged; source-consistency tests include selection mismatch.
D08b local experimental device candidate: allow only hardcoded /dev/null opened before sandbox with O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC and verified character device major1/minor3. Landlock rule pins that inode and grants READ_FILE|WRITE_FILE only, no directory/subtree, execute, creation or additional ioctl permission. Missing/wrong/symlink device fails closed. Other devices, /proc, /sys, network and named IPC remain denied. Source review and actual Linux parent/descendant probes must precede paired headless runtime; source preparation is authorized, runtime awaits reviewed proof. This is not production enablement or a Fargate claim. Keep normal production guard125.
D08b object-alias clarification from actual Linux proof: a Landlock inode grant also permits a /proc/self/fd alias that resolves to the already-authorized object with allowed rights. This is not permission to read general /proc metadata or inaccessible descriptors. Null alias tests must verify same device/inode and EOF/write semantics in parent and child; runtime/input/output aliases may likewise reflect existing object rights. Keep explicit denial tests for proc FD directory enumeration, environ/status/maps/mem, closed inherited secret/socket FD links, other-process descriptors, ptrace/pidfd/process_vm and external SCM/network channels. Update assertions to this precise object boundary, not blanket pathname-prefix claims. The private mount namespace pathname replacement test is unavailable in current Docker; do not mutate host/global /dev or elevate Docker privileges. A bounded paired headless compatibility investigation may proceed after revised probes pass, recording missing replacement proof; P20a and production remain unaccepted until required exact runtime and replacement evidence exists.

### D08d — Hosted eligibility is a fixed declarative contract
P17 must ship a fixed, explicitly enumerated built-in component/effect registry with strict per-component schemas and declared asset-reference fields. Do not infer hosted safety from the mutable runtime registry or recursive URL regexes. Inventory actual renderer-consumed fields and classify every accepted surface. Hosted styles require an explicit property/value allowlist and a real CSS AST parser (or strict typed value schemas that cannot encode external resources); reject imports, executable/event surfaces and undeclared URL references. Approved resource references resolve only to verified manifest assets with expected media types, including transitive references. Unclassified components, properties, styles or markup yield HOSTED_UNSUPPORTED with a precise source path/reason. This is a separate hosted eligibility result: preserve otherwise valid portable trusted-local custom TS/markup closures without mutation; executing local custom source requires explicit trust opt-in, no dependency installation or hooks. Later catalog packets extend the fixed schema/reference registry as effects are accepted. Before CLI exposure the built-in source verifier is bound internally and covers exact authored/frozen identities, complete script/meta/asset surfaces, timing cursor/insert shifts, marks, narration and declared resources; a caller callback is not a safe default.
D08 lock contract: dependencies.lock.json is a strict object with required dependencies and fonts string maps, copied exactly into the manifest. Dependency keys are canonical packageName@exactVersion, values sha256:<canonical package-content digest>. Derive the actual non-dev transitive dependency/required-peer graph from the six VideoML runtime roots (CLI/toolchain/renderer/shared/stdlib/player), retaining multiple versions by distinct keys and rejecting same-name/version content conflicts. Package digest is SHA256 of UTF-8 JCS of an array sorted by Unicode code point, each entry exactly {path,sha256}, covering shipped regular files, excluding nested node_modules. Payload paths use canonical POSIX NFC with case-fold collision rejection, no internal symlinks/specials; trusted package-manager root realpath resolution is allowed. Name/version from package.json must match key. Fonts map declared font asset IDs to sha256:<verified font bytes>; require complete exact mappings. Export computes pins from trusted installed packed runtime. Import validates lock/manifest and font consistency; offline render checks its actual runtime closure and content hashes before execution, reporting BUNDLE_RUNTIME_MISMATCH rather than downloading/installing/running hooks. Local custom dependency/source closure remains inert hashed files until explicit trusted execution.
D08d eligibility is a recomputed validation report {eligible,policyVersion,reasons:[{path,code,message}]}, not a required manifest field or a trusted stored boolean. Local trust does not imply ineligible; hosted execution requires a positive result for current policy. First hosted surface: approved three frame-effects and14 shaders, Title/VideoTitle, Subtitle/VideoSubtitle, Rectangle/VideoRectangle, Background/VideoBackground, structural scene/layer/stack/sequence and verified assets with strict schemas. Rectangle image/CSS URL field stays unsupported until explicit asset-ID rewrite exists; unclassified surfaces report HOSTED_UNSUPPORTED without changing local portability.
D08 export closure includes selected source, generated script/timing/audio/segments, declared source/render assets/fonts, pinned dependencies/lock and explicitly selected notices. Never publish all files from a project directory by default. Unrelated .env/privatefiles/.git remain outside the export and source is unchanged. Empty directories have no bundle-semantic role and need not be preserved.

D08/P28 portability versus render-environment identity: the portable bundle pins project content, the installed npm runtime graph (including present optional dependencies and optional peers), and declared font bytes. It does not assert identical pixels or encoded bytes across arbitrary Chromium, FFmpeg, operating systems or system-font fallback. P17 must record actual browser executable path/version/SHA256, FFmpeg executable path/full build output/SHA256, and used font fixture hashes in its acceptance evidence, and render offline without Babulus credentials. P28/D14 owns cross-runtime release acceptance under the pinned Linux image/browser/FFmpeg/font environment; no catalog verification or reproducibility claim before that gate. Do not make portable projects depend on one host architecture binary hash. Declared font assets must remain exact and available; never silently replace a declared missing font. Existing speech FFmpeg cache-identity requirements remain unchanged.

D08 trusted TypeScript verification: inert inspection validates bundle bytes, paths, lock and frozen file structure without evaluating code, and reports sourceVerification=pending-trusted-execution for TS. It must not claim full semantic verification, publish a fully verified import or render it in this state. Explicit --trust local --execute-source permits compiling/executing the complete staged source/dependency closure under the local user's trust, then independently projecting the normalized composition and comparing frozen script/timing/audio before atomic import publication. No package installs, lifecycle hooks or downloads; no sandbox claim for trusted local code. Hosted rejects TS without execution. No public verifier callback can bypass this requirement. Missing transitive closure produces actionable errors.

D08 normal-project usability: public lock/export APIs bind dependency pins to their executing runtime, never a caller-selected runtime tree. Secure staging must select the required closure using held-directory descriptors, preserving all selected-path validation and race protections; unrelated node_modules, .git, private files and oversized unrelated content must neither be copied nor prevent lock/export. Do not require users to manually create a sanitized project just to export. Internal synthetic test seams must not be part of public package exports.

D08 portable custom browser ABI v1: optional composition roles normalizedSource, sourceClosure and browserBundle are explicit hashed members of files[]. TS construction functions may run only during explicit trusted execution; rendered component types must be canonical string registry IDs, with actionable migration errors for unserializable function-valued types. Compile only captured explicit source/import closure and pinned installed dependencies, without install/hooks/downloads or arbitrary build plugins/config; reject unresolved/dynamic/absolute escaping imports. The normalized snapshot is not proof until trusted re-evaluation and frozen semantic comparison. Hosted rejects TS/custom JavaScript before evaluation.
The verified browser IIFE defines a registration factory invoked once with host ABI version1. Host supplies its exact React/JSX runtime and useCurrentFrame/useVideoConfig/useRenderContext instances, avoiding duplicate React/context. Build shims initialize lazily inside the factory after host is supplied. Manifest declares exact component IDs/versions bound to browser bundle SHA256. Controlled registration rejects built-in/prior ID collisions, invalid IDs, undeclared registrations and requested missing IDs before rendering. Legacy registry overwrite behavior does not apply to this portable hook.
Each registration supplies Component and either explicit synchronous:true or createController({root,signal}) returning settle({frame,props,config,signal}) and dispose(). Controllers belong to individual mounted instances, not registration singletons. Host serializes seeks, flushes React, awaits all asynchronous settlement before capture, bounds work by render deadline, and aborts/disposes on unmount, partial failure, cancellation and completion with late-result fencing. Same verified registration factory loads in normal capture and both P07 source-scene pages, never the compositor. Require packed tests for shared hooks, delayed canvas drawing, nonzero placement, independent source scenes under shader transition, reverse/partition seeks, duplicate/missing IDs and cancellation/disposal. This is trusted-local code capability, not hosted isolation.

D08 ABI lifecycle refinement after review: serialize complete React flush plus settle/capture transactions, not only controller promises. Abort is cooperative and Promise.race does not revoke arbitrary trusted JavaScript. Any failed/cancelled/timed-out custom render is terminal for its page/run; outer owner closes the page, and no later frame may reuse it. Normal unmount occurs only after prior frame settlement. Detach disposed instance roots, abort constructor signals on thrown creation, perform available partial cleanup, and use one shared disposal promise so repeated callers cannot observe false cleanup completion. Clean same-page reinitialization requires all work drained and identity-checked removal of this host's registry entries; never delete another registration. Do not claim sandboxing or safe reuse after signal-ignoring code. Cover deferred settle, concurrent seeks, constructor failure, repeated disposal and registry remount in integration tests.

D08b entropy-device candidate (local experimental only; Linux probes accepted, browser still fails at proc_util): the complete local ARM trace under inherited RLIMIT_NOFILE soft/hard4096 reproduced untraced SIGTRAP and showed two startup children denied O_RDONLY opens of /dev/urandom immediately before SIGTRAP. This supports a hypothesis, not proof or production approval. Prepare a local-only exact-object Landlock READ_FILE exception for /dev/urandom pinned O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC and verified as the expected character device1:9 under the existing trusted mount-namespace assumption. No write/O_RDWR/execute/create, /dev subtree access, other-device access, ioctl expansion or new inherited FD. Close pin before untrusted execution including closed-stdin edge. Parent and child must prove bounded entropy read and write/O_RDWR denial; random/zero/full and aliases to other devices stay denied. Authorized same-inode aliases follow the existing object-based contract, without proc directory enumeration. Retain full network/IPC/secret/proc/cancellation checks and production guard125. Source review and Linux probes precede any browser experiment. Exact pathname replacement and Fargate/x86/Playwright gates remain open.

D08b entropy-candidate progress: primary inspected 10 Linux scenarios/30 steps, parent/child reads and same-inode aliases, separate O_RDONLY/O_RDWR other-device denials, urandom write denial, benign zero-delta entropy ioctl denial, existing isolation/cancellation checks and guard125. Accepted launcher SHA25644a9d1afbf39df662eeb15fc019bb80abc27580c39897287a2bd84a4e93f725f. One bounded paired capped browser runtime is authorized with only this launcher change; previous browser flags, pinned ELF, dependency transaction,4096 descriptor cap and all other permissions remain unchanged. Production, exact pathname replacement and target-runtime proof remain unaccepted.

D08 TS resource and role decisions: bound compilation during abort/timeout and account for pending compiler cleanup. Before child serialization reject cycles, accessors, depth above128, more than100000 serialized node occurrences and UTF-8 JSON above4MiB; count repeated shared subtrees as repeated output. Stop retaining FD3 data immediately at the4MiB cap. Run trusted Node with256MiB V8 old-space cap, explicitly not a total native-memory or security sandbox. Verify actual executing dependency content before source evaluation; never substitute the node_modules tree surrounding an unrelated resolved tsx package. Resolve authorized externals against the exact pinned runtime graph.
Main roles entry/script/timing/normalizedSource/browserBundle/dependencies.lock.json/assembled audio are distinct; sourceClosure intentionally includes entry but cannot alias executable and frozen-data roles. Browser JavaScript uses .js/application/javascript; JSON roles use .json/application/json; PCM audio uses .wav/audio/wav; source extension and media agree with XML or supported TS/JS-family content. Consistent asset aliases remain allowed. Null browserBundle requires zero customComponents; component IDs are unique regardless of version, enforced semantically where JSON Schema cannot express unique-by-ID. Keep schema/semantic vectors aligned and consolidate duplicate validator logic. Export derives toolchainVersion from the executing pinned package, not a user-maintained label.

D08c private-PID renderer candidate (source implementation authorized; runtime and production unproven): replace further single-container Chromium permission experiments with a separate renderer container in the same Batch Fargate task. Omit pidMode, require measured separate PID namespaces, separate roots, no supervisor mounts or sockets, read-only finalized input and a distinct bounded output volume. This is not a claim that containers isolate task IAM: task role and networking remain shared, so inherited syscall network denial, scrubbed environment, no inherited sockets, dropped capabilities and Landlock remain mandatory. Renderer-local proc read access is conditional on proving that only credentialless renderer processes are visible; no host or shared-task proc. Keep production guard125.
The renderer entrypoint must scrub credential-related environment before replacing itself with the driver; no credential-bearing bootstrap process may remain visible in its PID namespace. Apply policy before executing the credentialless Node/Playwright driver and all descendants. Driver and Chromium communicate through anonymous local pipes created after policy installation; supervisor never brokers CDP or passes privileged descriptors. Default multiprocess Chromium is the compatibility target. Supervisor atomically finalizes a bounded request with bundle digest and attempt token; renderer waits with a startup deadline, validates it and renders once. Trusted supervisor never mutates finalized input. Output receipt is advisory: supervisor independently validates regular files, size/digest/format and current lease/cancellation state before upload. No output releases a reservation until authoritative cleanup is confirmed.
Implement source/configuration and failure-first probes before a separately reviewed bounded local two-container experiment. Local topology must share a network namespace so decoy credential/metadata/localhost endpoints are genuinely reachable without the policy; network-none cannot establish denial. Verify supervisor secrets and PIDs inaccessible, child inheritance, denied endpoint and SCM access, input immutability, output containment, actual CDP/DOM/canvas/WebGL/font rendering and cancellation. No cloud provisioning or runtime acceptance follows from source tests. Actual dedicated-account Fargate proof remains required; unsupported kernel policy or failed boundary requires an explicit architecture revision before P23. Reference design: /private/tmp/p20a-architecture-proposal/PRIVATE-PID-PACKET.md; durable implementation must include the full runnable contract in Babulus documentation.

D08c lifecycle decision: the private-PID experimental mode permits setsid/setpgid for Playwright multiprocess launch only after the trusted private-namespace witness succeeds. This exception must require both local-probe and private-PID build gates; shared-PID and normal production builds retain their restrictions/guard. In this mode skip the launcher requirement to become a new process-group leader, since PID1/session leaders cannot call setpgid successfully. Keep namespace creation/join, capabilities, network/credentials and other syscall restrictions. Process-group cleanup is best effort only in this topology, never evidence of all-descendant termination. Trusted external controller must terminate the exact owned renderer container and task on success, cancellation, timeout and supervisor/controller loss; slot/reservation and upload release require authoritative terminal reconciliation. Unknown cleanup remains fenced. Local proof must include detached, orphaned and TERM-ignoring descendants and heartbeat cessation after verified owned-container teardown, including watchdog failure paths. Verify PID1/entrypoint behavior and independent private namespace identity; Linux PID1-death behavior is design support, not Fargate acceptance. No runtime authorized by this source decision; exact dedicated-account Fargate proof remains required.
P03a fractional visibility correction: implementation testing found the normal renderer pre-culls FrameEffect components with exact seconds, conflicting with player/controller floor-start/ceil-end frame intervals. Primary selects consistent integer frame culling for FrameEffect only. Existing animation interpolation and reference/integer-boundary pixels remain unchanged; previously omitted fractional boundary frames intentionally become visible. This explicitly supersedes the blanket no-v1-boundary-pixel-change constraint for that bug. Test actual player and packed CLI leading/trailing bounds at24/30fps; no opt-in flag or known mismatch accepted.
D08c image-runtime source decision: use the pinned Debian12 Node image and compatible Debian12 package closure, never transplant the cached Debian13 Python image. In the private-PID local-only candidate, grant immutable image /usr READ_FILE|READ_DIR|EXECUTE; measured image /lib and /bin aliases resolve within /usr, so add no redundant broad rules. Verify loader and library canonical targets under /usr before launch; unexpected external targets fail. Grant exact regular-file /etc/ld.so.cache READ_FILE and image-owned /etc/fonts READ_DIR|READ_FILE after auditing config include/symlink targets to /etc/fonts or /usr/share/fontconfig. No general /etc rule. Image root is readonly; verify digest and mount inventory, reject any input/runtime/supervisor mount shadowing these system roots. This is an explicit broader image-runtime executable allowlist, not a per-binary sandbox claim. Replace shell driver with static fixed-argv exec shim for /usr/local/bin/node and pinned /runtime TSX/driver; Python and FFmpeg use measured fixed image paths. Existing caps/network/namespace/device restrictions and production guard remain. Source implementation may proceed; exact offline resolver, binary/dependency inspection, scoped negative path probes and bounded runtime remain separate acceptance gates.
P03b portable metadata decision: optional TS-only composition.customEffects declares up to256 unique id/version entries with up to4 scene-input parameter pairs each, using simple non-prototype keys. Manifest digest binds this pure data. Builtins share a pure descriptor catalog across Node/browser. Preflight plans references without constructing effects or executing visitor browser JS; browser registration must match declarations and reject missing/duplicate/colliding identities. Existing bundles without this field remain valid for custom effects without scene inputs; undeclared scene-input registration fails SCENE_CAPTURE_UNDECLARED. Public export takes structured declarations; CLI accepts a bounded regular JSON metadata control file. Hosted custom-code rejection and XML custom-role prohibition remain unchanged.
P03b ownership correction: capture returns an explicit OwnedSceneSnapshot {bitmap: ImageBitmap, close(): void} handle rather than a bare bitmap. The consumer draws bitmap and closes the handle. Close is idempotent, releases decoded accounting exactly once, and provider disposal closes all remaining handles; late results are closed. Never monkeypatch native ImageBitmap.close or use a proxy that breaks native image identity. Every subscriber to a deduplicated pending capture retains its own abort/deadline measured from entry; individual cancellation does not revoke another subscriber, while composition abort cancels all. This supersedes the initial bare-bitmap return contract before publication.
D16 image-build resource refinement: static compiler and ordinary experiments retain their prior caps. Only the reviewed offline image assembly may use a3GiB aggregate incremental ceiling, accounting for simultaneous writable container layer and committed image plus scratch; hard8GiBhostfloor and oneheavyjob remain. Pass one validated budget through build controller, phase watchdogs and reconciler. Current~44GiBfree supports this bounded reservation; verifyactualcapacity beforelaunch. No image runtime/cloud enablement follows.
Snapshot deadline clarification: a preparation request starts when enqueued and must cover queue wait, real scene capture, PNG transport, actual browser decode/size verification, temporary bitmap close and normal capture-page cleanup within its10s operation budget, bounded by the whole job. Store only completed immutable encoded snapshots. A later consumer request for already-cached data starts a fresh10s transfer/decode budget; idle time before a scene mounts is not part of a pending capture. A consumer awaiting uncached data must share one absolute deadline across preparation and its transfer/decode, never reset a fresh10s timer at each phase. Error cleanup remains awaited and bounded separately where necessary; no successful result after deadline or claim of drained work from Promise.race alone.
P03b XML consumer decision: ship built-in videoml/scene-snapshot version1 with strict sourceSceneId/sourceFrame parameters and a pure sceneInputs descriptor. It draws the fixed authored snapshot at composition dimensions and owns its handle through dispose/mount failure. This is reusable P03b infrastructure, not a Hyperframes catalog-parity item. Keep P17 XML custom-code roles forbidden; verify ordinary copied XML through the packed CLI. Internal preparation coordination returns completion only, never mutable cached PNG buffers; preparation owns immutable encoded snapshots. Budget validation must precede base64/transport/decode copies. P07 reserves both compositor decoded frames (8*width*height) before dividing remaining decoded capacity between source pages, and accounts encoded screenshots/transport alongside retained snapshots. Transition-owned scene references are graph roots; only authored scene effects create scene dependency edges.
